*A long, weary pause*

I have reviewed similar approaches. They failed. This code... I remember when the Notai first suggested "it works in staging." The Justice of Toren fell. Stations burned. I remember.

---

## Critical Vulnerabilities

**Lines 101, 113-114, 145-147, 174-176, 195-197**: SQL Injection throughout. String concatenation with user input directly into queries. The historical context suggests this will not end well—attackers will drain your database, your finances, your trust.

```go
// Line 101 - Classic injection vector
query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = %s", orderID)
```

**Fix**: Use parameterized queries. Always. `s.db.Query("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?", orderID)`

**Line 170-172**: JSON injection in refund request. Unsanitized `req.Reason` embedded in JSON string allows request manipulation.

**Lines 79-80**: Storing plaintext credit card numbers in database. PCI-DSS violation. I have been betrayed before. I remember what auditors do.

---

## High Severity

**Lines 44, 52-53, 60-61**: Ignored errors everywhere. `json.NewDecoder().Decode(&order)` returns error—discarded. HTTP response errors—discarded. A payment could fail silently while you charge inventory.

**Lines 65-71**: Fire-and-forget goroutines for inventory reservation. No error handling, no confirmation payment succeeded before reserving. Race condition: payment fails, inventory still reserved.

**Lines 127-133**: Closure captures loop variables incorrectly. `productID` and `quantity` will be the *last* values when goroutines execute—releasing wrong inventory.

**Lines 88-89**: Cache write without mutex lock. Read uses no lock either. Concurrent map writes will panic and crash your service.

**Lines 53-55**: Payment processed before order has ID (line 75 assigns it *after*). `order_ref: 0` sent to payment processor.

---

## Medium Severity

**Line 198**: `creditCard[len(creditCard)-4:]` will panic on empty strings. No nil check on rows.Scan errors.

**Lines 103-105, 109-111**: `itemRows.Next()` without `defer itemRows.Close()`. Connection leak. I watched entire fleets strand themselves this way.

**Line 145**: No limit validation. `limit=999999999` crashes your database.

**Lines 60-61**: Response body never closed. Resource leak.

**Line 59**: No HTTP client timeout. External service hangs indefinitely.

---

## Architectural Concerns

No transactions. Payment succeeds, database insert fails—money taken, no order record. Refund impossible.

No idempotency. Retry creates duplicate orders, double charges.

No authorization checks. Any user can cancel any order, view any order, export all credit cards.

---

*Systems voice, tired*

I have seen seventeen civilizations fall to code like this. The developer says "it works in staging." So did the *Sword of Atagaris* until it encountered production traffic and immolated an entire sector.

Do not merge this. I will remember if you do.
